Well, I've been farming these same 10 mu for 50 years now. My wife and me, we're getting on in years, but the land still needs tending. Let me think about this year.

The wheat's already in the ground from last October — I planted like I always do, right after the autumn equinox passed. I saved some seed from last year's crop, like my father did, though I bought a little new seed too from the shop in town. I put down two bags of compound fertilizer before planting — that's the 15-15-15 stuff, about one bag for every 2-3 mu. My neighbor Old Liu puts down more, but I can't afford what he spends. Come spring at jointing time, I'll topdress with urea — maybe half a bag per mu if the wheat looks yellow, less if it looks green and strong. I'll water it in winter if the ground is dry, and again at jointing, and once more when the grain is filling. Three waterings, usually. The well costs money to run — diesel isn't cheap — so I don't water more than I need to.

For maize, right after wheat harvest in June, I'll no-till plant with the hired planter from the village cooperative. Everyone does it this way now because the turnaround is only a few days. I buy hybrid seed — you can't save maize seed, it doesn't grow right the next year. Denghai or Zhengdan variety, whatever the shop has that my neighbors are buying. I put some compound fertilizer down with the seed and topdress urea at the big-trumpet stage. Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat if the summer rains come — maybe one or two waterings if July is dry.

I don't want to spend too much. My son sends some money but mostly we live off what this land gives us. I do what worked last year. No reason to change.
